exact_statement: For every finite balanced disjoint Boolean composition tree with literal leaves or a balanced stopping frontier, delta(F)=sum_internal J(v)delta(g_v)+sum_terminal J(l)delta(Sub_l), and sum_internal J(v)Lambda(g_v)<= (4+6/e)[delta(F)-sum_terminal J(l)delta(Sub_l)] in nats. The exact first-charge factorization is Lambda(F)=sum_internal A(v)sum_i alpha_vi^2 ln(1/alpha_vi^2)W1(Sub_vi)+sum_terminal A(l)Lambda(Sub_l). In contrast no finite K bounds sum_nonroot c J(c)Lambda(Sub_c) by K I(F): the rare-switch chain with depth d=2^(2k), r=3k, p=2^(-3k) has I<=5/2 and that bank/I >=2^k(1-2^(-2k))/5 for k>=2. The same Boolean family satisfies H(F)<=6(I(F)-1) in bits.
hypotheses: Uniform finite cubes and normalized Fourier coefficients; Boolean sign functions.
Gate outputs and child/subformula outputs are balanced; physical child blocks are disjoint.
J(v) is the product of ancestor gate coordinate influences; A(v) is the product of ancestor singleton coefficients squared.
Lambda uses nats, H uses bits, delta=I-1; no depth or arity bound. No physical-restriction transfer is asserted.
